title: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom
Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
Crash Bandicoot
review: So this game was our game of the month for September, we played the NSane Trilogy version. i had played the original games on Playstation1 - in fact it is probably one of the games i remember best from our Ps1 growing up. The game is just as I remembered but with a new skin which is neat. Crash was one of playstations attempts to take a part of nintendo’s market during the ‘mascot platforming” craze of the 90s/00s. Now hear me out, I love platformers - but I just dont think this is a very good one. Hilarious when people call this a souls like, but it does have that feeling of difficult frustration and having to start all the way at the beginning of shit. But thats about as close to souls as it gets imo. The scope of the mechanics is just so narrow, the closest thing I can relate it to is the mobile games Flappy Bird or Temple Run.. A couple of the bosses toward the end were fun and the character designs were fantastic as well. I like the character of crash and respect his legacy, but the gameplay just had me wishing for more an so thats why I put it at Number 23

title: Dark Souls II
review:
This was the last souls game that I hadnt played or beaten
Mixed bag of  opinions, I liked the story and atmosphere a lot - it reminded me of Demon's Souls so much
I eventually got over the ADP and general jankiness and grew to love the combat systems the game had to offer
But the worst part of the game, making me to NOT wanna go back to it any time soon, is the bull shit game design choices in most areas - tons of annoying key items to find, overcrowded with enemies, which then start to despawn?? Like if they had to add that to the game then you know they had the difficulty tuned horribly before they added that mechanic in. Felt like I was fighting big crowds most the times I died..

title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
review:

The perfect Harry Potter RPG would be a giant fleshed out version of the winterhold questline imo
FUCKING SHITTY UI
hype menu music
Obviously an undeniable MEGACHAD when it comes to RPGS
The RPG formula of the Elder Scrolls games shines through in this game. but in my late adaption playthrough, it made me excited about the formula overall more than anything else

title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
What Remains of Edith Finch
review:
Very immersive
quite depressing
Amazing just finished it and I choked up a bit
I view it as an allegory for death. In a sense we all have the “Finch” curse and the narrator’s (Edith) message is that we should be amazed and grateful for the time we have instead of saddened by the time we might lose
Beautiful storytelling.
I wish I used a controller for it, felt a little odd on mkb
with a controller I would even have anybody experience this, to show how artistic games can be
The switch in gameplay style while telling stories of her relatives was so cool and felt very hip and refreshing
THe fish cutting scene is so rememorable (wrote this 6 months later) - favorite sibling

title: Shin Megami Tensei V
review:
long as fuck and grindy... but ADDICTING
amazing systems and types/statuses
makes me worried that all other JRPGs will feel inferior..
The battles are absolutely top tier, but its making me realize there is a small part of me that wants a little bit more of a story... idk if it even effects the fun factor necessarily but makes it feel more worthwhile perhaps
Im sold on the SMT family of games
press turn, moon cycles, demon fusion, its all so fucking sick and instantly feels classic
You know I went down a SMT rabbit hole on youtube since playing this game...
The final battles were epic and i won the final fight with just naho
maybe replay some day → it will always be my first atlus game

title: Metroid Prime Remastered
review: I like the gameplay but it seems to have a ceiling of enjoyment for me. All the weapon and suit upgrades are awesome and add new aspects to gameplay, similar to Metroid Dread. My least favorite upgrades though, were the visors, which were used for a lot of different areas for platforming and puzzle solving. It definitely worked and fits for the first person perspective, but the awesome God-like movement you have at the end of Dread is much more preferable to me than switching between visors and weapon colors. Not too mention there is no SHINE SPARK!!
